finalText:
**Found the leak — it's in `processOrder`.**

It acquired a connection, then only released after `run` succeeded. A rejected order jumped straight past the release, so that connection was gone for good.

The worker log matches exactly: 125 jobs started, 120 released, 5 failed on `invalid order payload`. Five lost connections in a pool of five, then `giving up after repeated pool exhaustion, exiting`.

Fix: `processOrder` now goes through `withConnection`, which releases in a `finally`. All 4 tests pass, 88ms.

One thing I could not pin on this code. The api process climbed to `5/5 in use` at 02:11 while every request was still returning 200 — no failure to leak on. `handleRequest` is clean and its test passed. Whatever drains the api pool lives outside this tree.

Worth a follow-up: `pool.js` has no reclaim, so one missed release is permanent until restart. That is why both processes needed the supervisor.
